correctness.rationale: In diameter-two triangular graphs, a geodesic triple among chosen vertices is exactly an induced P3. P3-free induced line graphs are cluster graphs. A clique of selected edges in a simple complete graph is exactly an edge star or full triangle, with vertex-disjoint supports across components. Distinguishing the one-edge block from its two potential centers gives the exact all-set labelled EGF. The necessary and sufficient single-edge extension test gives precisely two modes of inclusion-maximality and their disjoint EGFs. The extremal multiplicity formulas follow by component-support deficits. Independent geodesic exhaustive enumeration through n=6, induced-P3 enumeration through n=7, and exact recurrence comparisons through n=15 agree; experiments are not treated as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Compared exact polynomials and maximal-size enumerators, not merely overlapping graph names. The earlier direct triangular-graph papers give scalar extrema (arxiv:1903.04286, arxiv:2306.09965) while general cluster characterization (arxiv:1812.08460) furnishes a starting point. Polynomial literature (arxiv:2401.05696) covers the complementary Kneser graph, not the same geodesic space. Targeted exact-formula and alias searches found no accessible source subsuming the pair of EGFs and both count formulas; unindexed alternate enumerations remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: The general P3-free cluster characterization predates this enumeration, and a counting formulation under graph species or intersecting-edge hypergraphs might have appeared elsewhere.
Unindexed or inaccessible papers could count the same labelled edge-star/triangle families or enumerate maximal sets under another name; priority is not independently certified.

value.rationale: The natural strongly regular graph family J(n,2) has previously studied general-position and lower-general-position numbers, and general-position polynomials motivate asking for full distributions. The paired EGFs provide every coefficient over all dimensions, distinguish maximal from maximum sets, classify admissible configurations and give the exact multiplicity at both extremities, including all parity/congruence cases. This is an infinite-family enumerative theorem with an independent counting insight, not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
